description.narrative: Rehabilitation of 4 community/institutional water sources inBusano village, Busiu village, Busiyangp primary school andMutese primary school all located in Busano sub county inMabale district. • Procurement and installation of 2 water tanksfor water harvesting in2 schools of Bubuyagu and Namubutyeprimary schools in Mbale local government. • Training of (40)members of governance disaggregatedas 10 members ofwater user committee members, 10 members of Village HealthTeams and 20 members of school management clubs toensure governance of the facilities. Project Context /Background[maximum words -200] Uganda is vulnerable to the impacts of climate change,experiencing shorter or longer rains and harsher droughts, whichpresent a threat to the ecosystem and people’s livelihoods.Mbale district in Mount Elgon region is one of the regions proneto disasters associated with heavy rainfall such as landslides andfl oods andthese disasters impact the lives and livelihood of thepeople by contamination of water sources used by bothcommunities and institutions. This situation limits access to water,sanitary facilities, due to over dependency in utilisation of surfacerun off springs. These are the only existing water sources and areat risk of contamination due to proximity to fi lled latrines. Theimpact is also exacerbated by destruction of infrastructure suchas gravity fl ow schemes and water supply pipes, property and road network cut off due to fl oods and landslides thathappened on late August 2025, Elgon region was also hit byintense rainfall that lasted for several hours resulting in fl ashfl oods, and mudslides, as a result, several riverbanks busted dueto the heavy downpour. The affected parisheswere Bufukhula,Nyondo in Nyondo Sub County, Bwihonje, Buyaka, Busano andBufooto in Busano Sub Counties in Mbale district. Followingthisdisaster comprising landslides, fl oods, and windstorms in anarea already vulnerable to natural disasters and shocks,signifi cant damage occurred to water-related infrastructure.Surface runoff springs are currently the only source of water, yetthey remain at high risk of contamination due to their locationand exposure. These risks are worsened by the proximity of fi lledlatrines to the springs. Assessments were done to inform aresponse. Project Aims /Objectives [maximumwords - 200] The project aims at enhancing water supply in the impactedarea. We will protect the existing water springs used bycommunities and institutions, support water treatment and waterquality monitoring. We will also l install 2 water storage tanks ininstitutions such as primary schools and procure and pre-position 15 Diethyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPD) tablets, providechlorine for water treatment, supporting the district waterdepartment to conduct detailed water quality monitoring andprovision of water collection and storage containers. Projectobjectives: 1. To provide clean and safe water through procuringand installation of 2 water harvesting tanks of 10,000 litters to 2primary schools in Bunkhoko sub county, Mbale district. 2. Torehabilitate or protect 4 community/institutional spring wells inBusano village, Busiu village,Busiyangp primary school andMutese primary school, all located in Busano sub county inMabale district. 3. To train 40 water user committee members inwater source management, resource mobilisation for Operationand Maintenance of the protected spring wells in Bunkhoko subcounty. 4. To procure and distribute 15 cartons of DPD (diethyl-p-phenylenediamine) tablets, provision of chlorine for watertreatment, support the district water department to conduct detailed water quality monitoring and provision of watercollection and storage containers. Project Deliverables /Outcomes / KeyBenefi ts [maximumwords - 200] 1. We will rehabilitate 4 community/institutional spring wells, andthis will target schools and health centres in disaster proneareas, to improve the supply of clean and safe water to pupils inprimary schools and patients in health care units. Rehabilitationand repair works will include replacement of fi ttings withretrofi tting parts and protection of embarkments andcatchment area. 2. We will procure and distribute 15 cartons ofwater treatment tablets to ensure access to clean and safedrinking water in communities whose water sources arecontaminated by faecal matter from submerged pit latrines. 3.We will install/rehabilitate 2 rainwater harvesting systems inseverely affected schools or other institutions. This will includeprocuring 2 tanks of 10,000 litre that will be elevated andconnectedto roof fl ow. The tanks will improve water catchmentfor iron sheet roofed houses. 4. We will procure and distribute20-litre jerry cans to 300 households severely affected by fl oodsand landslides. The jerry cans will not only ensure water storagebut alsoimprove water safety and cleanliness at householdlevel. 5. We will train total of 40 members (10 members of wateruser committee, 10 members of Village Health Teams and 20members of school management clubs to ensure governanceof the facilities.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
